what: THE DAILY BRIEF RENDERS AT 42 KB / 140 LINES AND IS THEREFORE UNREADABLE, AND THE MANAGER CAUSED IT. MEASURED 2026-09-21 on the first real render after A3a merged (9751e17): 42,159 characters, of which section 0 is the bulk. The GENERATOR is not at fault — it renders each pipeline item's `what` and `routed_to` verbatim, which is correct behaviour for a store whose fields are sentences. The fault is upstream: this manager wrote paragraph-length `routed_to` essays (one is 90+ words) and multi-hundred-word `what` fields, and section 0 prints them in full. [!] THIS IS A NEAR MISS OF THE EXACT FAILURE A8 WAS WARNED AGAINST. A8's acceptance test was that section 0 must not become a wall of undispositioned rows, and it passed — zero of its 607 promoted rows flood it. Mine is a wall of DISPOSITIONED rows, which is better in kind and identical in effect: an operator who will not read it gets the same nothing either way, and the whole mechanism rests on them reading it daily. [!] IT GETS WORSE, NOT BETTER, ON ITS OWN: A8's import takes the store to ~1,150 items and 87 currently-due, against the 7 rendered here. [!] TWO CANDIDATE FIXES AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT, so do not just pick one: (a) the brief TRUNCATES per-row text with the full text one click away — cheap, but this repo's rule is that a truncation must never be able to hide, so it needs the count printed beside it; (b) the STORE gets a length discipline — `what` is one sentence, the reasoning lives in the linked artifact. (b) is the real fix and (a) is the mitigation. Prefer (b), and note the validator currently enforces a minimum on these fields and no maximum.
